Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediCore Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Mike Chen, CFO; and Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MediCore Devices delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I'll cover four key aspects of our performance: our overall performance highlights and key achievements, organic revenue growth by segment and geography, hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates, and the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives. Mike will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Let's start with our overall performance highlights and key achievements. I'm thrilled with what we've accomplished this quarter, underscoring the strength and resilience of our diversified medical devices portfolio. We delivered record results across the board, exceeding our guidance and demonstrating successful execution of our Precision Growth 2025 strategy amid a dynamic macro environment.

On the top line, total revenue reached $1.28 billion, up 14% as reported and 12% on an organic constant currency basis, marking our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit organic growth. This beat our guidance midpoint by $30 million and came in ahead of consensus estimates. Robust procedure volumes grew 11% globally, fueled by the sustained rebound in elective surgeries post-COVID and our leadership in high-growth segments like structural heart and robotics.

Breaking it down by our four core pillars—Cardiovascular Solutions, Orthopedics & Spine, Advanced Surgical Technologies, and Diagnostics & Monitoring—here's where we saw the biggest wins. Cardiovascular Solutions, our largest segment at 42% of revenue, delivered $538 million, up 16% organically. Structural heart shone brightly, with transcatheter mitral valve repair procedures up 22%, thanks to the continued rollout of our next-gen TMVR system, EchoValve II, which captured an incremental 1.5% market share versus competitors like Edwards Lifesciences' MitraClip. TAVR volumes grew 18%, benefiting from favorable CMS reimbursement updates and our expanded access program in ambulatory surgery centers.

Orthopedics & Spine generated $312 million, a solid 10% organic increase. Knee and hip implant average selling prices rose 4% due to premium pricing on our AI-optimized cementless implants, akin to Stryker's Mako advancements, while U.S. procedure volumes surged 13% as hospitals normalized backlogs. Our robotic-assisted knee platform hit a milestone with over 50,000 procedures performed year-to-date.

Advanced Surgical Technologies posted $285 million, up 15% organically, propelled by our da Vinci-like VersaBot robotic system, where the installed base grew 25% to 1,200 units globally. Utilization rates climbed to 92% from 88% a year ago, reflecting strong surgeon adoption and our new single-port capabilities that reduce OR time by 20%.

Diagnostics & Monitoring rounded out at $145 million, up 9%, with standout growth in our wearable cardiac monitors similar to Abbott's Confirm Rx, where subscription revenue from remote patient monitoring jumped 30% year-over-year.

On the bottom line, adjusted gross margins expanded 220 basis points to 69.2%, driven by a favorable mix shift toward high-margin robotics and supply chain efficiencies—we reduced resin and titanium costs by 8% through localized sourcing in Mexico and Vietnam. Operating income rose 22% to $385 million, with adjusted EPS of $1.52, surpassing our $1.42 guide and up 19% year-over-year. Free cash flow was a robust $420 million, enabling $150 million in share repurchases and a 10% dividend hike announced today.

Key achievements position us for sustained leadership. First, regulatory momentum: We secured FDA approval for our AI-powered intravascular imaging platform, ClearSight AI, which enhances PCI outcomes by 15% in lesion detection accuracy—early adopter data mirrors the impact of Philips' Volcano tech. In Europe, we earned CE Mark for our neuromodulation device targeting chronic pain, entering a $5 billion total addressable market growing at 12% CAGR.

Second, innovation pipeline acceleration: R&D investment hit $210 million, or 16.4% of revenue—up from 15% last year—with 12 investigational device exemptions filed year-to-date. Our technical initiatives include integrating generative AI for predictive maintenance on robotic systems, reducing downtime by 30%, and advancing tele-proctoring platforms to scale surgeon training amid global talent shortages.

Third, strategic M&A and partnerships: We closed the $450 million acquisition of NeuroPulse Therapeutics, bolstering our hypertension modulation portfolio with their FDA Breakthrough Designation device, positioning us against Medtronic's Symplicity Spyral. Internationally, our JV with a top Chinese distributor expanded VersaBot access, targeting 20% China med device market growth.

Regionally, the U.S. led with 16% organic growth, comprising 58% of revenue, as elective procedure volumes normalized to 105% of pre-pandemic levels and ASC penetration hit 35% for our orthopedics line. EMEA grew 8%, tempered by single-digit pricing pressures in Germany and France under HTA scrutiny, but offset by strong structural heart performance.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography. Excluding the impacts of our recent NeuroVance Therapeutics acquisition and about 2% foreign exchange headwinds, we delivered 12% organic revenue growth year-over-year, accelerating from prior quarters and reflecting robust procedural demand, favorable mix shifts toward high-acuity devices, and early traction from new product introductions.

By segments, Cardiovascular, at 42% of revenue, grew organically by 16%, with structural heart as our North Star—TAVR volumes up 18% globally via our next-gen AetherValve Pro, capturing 220 basis points of U.S. market share against Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien. Coronary intervention grew 9%, driven by our drug-eluting stent portfolio, including CE Mark for AetherStent Nano with improved deliverability in complex lesions. Electrophysiology added 10%, benefiting from our AI-enhanced mapping system reducing procedure times by 15%, akin to Biosense Webster's CARTO with proprietary machine learning for ablation guidance.

Orthopedics and Spine, 28% of revenue, saw 10% organic growth. Hip and knee reconstruction surged 14% as volumes hit 105% of 2019 levels. Our robotic-assisted AetherOrtho R1, with haptic feedback like Stryker's Mako, drove 25% sub-franchise growth post-July U.S. launch. Spine grew 6%, mitigated by 12% ASP uplift on expandable interbody fusion devices.

Diabetes Management, 15% of revenue, posted 9% growth despite GLP-1 headwinds, similar to Dexcom and Tandem. CGM sensors rose 11%, with AetherLink implantable hitting 50,000 units, gaining share from Abbott's FreeStyle Libre via 14-day accuracy. Insulin delivery was stable, with patch pump pipeline integrating iOS HealthKit for 2025 acceleration.

Vision and Other, 22% of revenue including ophthalmology and endoscopy, delivered 9% growth. Intraocular lenses up 8% post extended-depth-of-focus IOL launch versus Alcon's Vivity; endoscopy offset Japan pricing via 15% single-use adoption.

Geographically, U.S. business—68% of revenue—led with 16% organic growth, propelled by CMS expansions for TAVR and robotics, plus 3% ASP from GPO renewals. Procedural growth outpaced IDC by 300 basis points, with 1,200+ clinical specialists boosting OR utilization.

EMEA, 18% of revenue, grew 8% organically, strong in Germany and UK from CE Marks, tempered by 4% FX; structural heart gained in Italy TAVR centers.

APAC, 10%, fastest at 11.5%, China rebounding 15% via SinoMed JV on cardio consumables. Japan 8% from endoscopy; India/ASEAN 20%+ on ortho kits.

Latin America/Canada grew 4.2%, Brazil recovery offsetting Argentina.

This underscores our Procedural Excellence framework: 8% revenue in R&D for NPIs like neuromodulation burst therapy—FDA breakthrough filing next quarter—and ASC footprint at 22% ortho volumes. AetherCloud connects 4,500 ORs, with software subscriptions up 30%.

We expect Q4 organic growth of 9-10%, accelerating in cardio and APAC with Medicare Advantage tailwinds, targeting 100bps annual share gains and 150bps margin expansion.

Moving on to hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates. Our flagship OmniFlex robotic-assisted platform, with FlexiArm articulation and AI-driven PrecisionGuide, drives strong uptake. In Q3, total placements grew 22% to 187 units: hospitals 62% mix at 116, up 18% YoY; ASCs surged 32% to 71. Sequential: hospitals 14.2% QoQ, ASCs 19.8%. U.S. hospital penetration 27% in high-volume cardiac/ortho centers like Cleveland Clinic, up from 21%; ASCs 16% in multi-specialty sites over 500 MIS annually, +5pts.

Recurring from FlexiTips consumables/service: $142 million, +28%; ASC utilization 2.8 procedures/system/week vs. 2.5 target, nearing da Vinci's 3.0+. ASP $1.82 million despite Medtronic Hugo/Stryker Mako pressure.

Trends: ASC shift via CMS site-neutral/2024 OPPS for TAVR/spinal; industry MIS +15%, we capture 24% ASC share vs. 12% hospitals. Hospitals prioritize capex efficiency; FlexLease converts 41% evaluations.

Q3 OmniFlex 3.0 software—haptic, 25% faster setup—cuts hysterectomies 17%. ASC kits like low-profile trocars +35% adoption. Premier/Vizient add 28 systems.

U.S. 78% placements, ASC +38% Sun Belt. Europe 14% to 24, Germany DRG/UK NHS. APAC China 12, Japan 5 ramping Q1'25; Brazil 4.

Doubling field specialists to 180 for high-ROC. Multi-specialty edge over J&J Ottava. Supply dual-sourcing <2% delays.

Q4 guide: hospitals 125, ASCs 82; FY +24%, 15-20% organic '25 vs. 12% market.

Finally, the impact of pricing and cost management initiatives. In this industry with CMS bundles, site-neutral policies, and Asian competition, these drove 250bps gross margin expansion to 69.2%, up 220bps YoY, with 12% core growth.

Pricing: 2.8% ASP increase via value-based, mix, GPO renewals.

Cardio/Structural: TAVR +3.5% on PROVE-IT data (22% lower reinterventions vs. Edwards Sapien); 85% Vizient/Premier premiums offset 4.2% NTAP cut.

Ortho/Robotics: +4.1% via Precision Pricing on 18% case time drops.

Diagnostics/CGM: +2.2% on CLARITY-2 A1c data vs. Abbott Libre.

U.S. +3.1% ASC shift (28% ortho outpatient +6pts); Europe +1.8% EU MDR/HTA; EM +4.5% China/India JVs. Pricing +1.4pts growth; 12 evidence dossiers for 2.5% FY25.

Costs: $52 million Q3 savings, 7.2% below prior COGS.

Supply: Global Sourcing 2.0 dual-sources 65% Vietnam/Mexico, -40% China; hedges titanium/polymers; $28 million, 15% resorbables like DuPont.

Manufacturing: Six Sigma 5.8% conversion cut; Galway pacemakers 92-97.5% yield; digital twins 11% material; Puerto Rico assembly -22% labor.

R&D/SG&A: AI design -25% cycles, 4% spend growth; ZBB -320bps, T&E -18%.

EMEA -8.1% Euro/inventories; APAC -9.4% Suzhou local.

Margin Resilience Framework aligns value-based/outpatient; 2.3x offset vs. Boston Scientific/Intuitive. FY24 pricing 1.5-2pts, $220 million cost run-rate. $1.2 billion cash for M&A neuromod. 12.4% EBITDA to $1.18 billion; 10-12% growth, 25%+ ROIC.

I will now turn the call over to Mike for a review of our financial results.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter. Revenue of $1.28 billion grew 14% reported, 12% organic, beating guidance. Gross margins hit 69.2%, +220bps from mix and efficiencies. Operating income $385 million, +22%; adjusted EPS $1.52, +19%. Free cash flow $420 million supported repurchases and dividend raise.

Expenses were well-controlled: R&D at 16.4% of revenue, SG&A deleveraged. For Q4, we guide revenue $1.32-$1.35 billion, organic 9-10%; EPS $1.55-$1.60. Full-year organic growth 11-12%, margins 68.5-69%. Long-term, 10%+ growth, 25% ROIC.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Mike. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex, on the structural heart strength, can you expand on EchoValve II market share gains and competitive dynamics with MitraClip?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. EchoValve II's next-gen design improved conformability and reduced leak rates, driving 22% procedure growth and 1.5% share gain. Versus MitraClip, our data shows better MR reduction at one year, resonating in high-volume centers. CMS updates helped TAVR too, with 18% volumes. We're gaining via evidence and ASC access—expect continued acceleration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. Mike, on cost savings, how sustainable are the supply chain wins, and any FX offset in Q4?

Mike Chen:
Emily, solid question. Global Sourcing 2.0 delivered $28 million from dual-sourcing and hedges—titanium down 8%, polymers 15%. Manufacturing automation like Galway yields ensure durability. Run-rate scales to $220 million by year-end. FX headwind ~2% Q4, but pricing +1.5-2pts offsets. Confident in 150bps leverage.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Thanks. Lena, on the AI integrations like ClearSight and predictive maintenance, what's the adoption pipeline and impact on robotics utilization?

Dr. Lena Patel:
David, thanks. ClearSight AI boosts PCI lesion detection 15%, with FDA approval sparking 20 early adopters mirroring Philips Volcano upside. Predictive AI on VersaBot/OmniFlex cuts downtime 30%, pushing utilization to 92%. Tele-proctoring scales training. Pipeline: 12 IDEs, neuromod burst filing soon. Expect 25% recurring software growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel:
Congrats team. Alex, thoughts on ASC penetration outlook and competitive positioning in robotics?

Alex Rivera:
Lisa, ASCs are key—35% ortho penetration, 16% overall up 5pts. OmniFlex 3.0's haptic/auto-docking cuts times 17-25%, utilization 2.8/week. Versus Hugo/Mako/Ottava, our multi-specialty wins 24% ASC share. Field team expansion to 180, GPO pipeline strong. Q4 82 ASC placements guide 15-20% '25 growth.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of MediCore Devices. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
